title: Growing from a seed
keyIdea: A seed is a baby plant with a packed lunch inside. Plant it in soil and give it water. In a warm place it wakes up: this is called germination. The root comes out first and grows down, even if the seed is upside down. Next the shoot grows up, and leaves open at the top. Seed, root, seedling, big plant: the big plant makes new seeds.

kid: A seed looks still, but there is a tiny plant inside. It has food packed in, like a lunch box.
Push the seed into the soil and give it water. In a warm room, the seed wakes up.
First a white root pops out. It always grows down, to drink water. Then a green shoot grows up. Leaves open at the top.
Now it is a seedling. With water and light it grows into a big plant. The big plant makes new seeds.
adult: In England, Development Matters (2023) asks 3 and 4 year olds to plant seeds and care for growing plants, and to understand the key features of the life cycle of a plant. Year 1 science names the basic structure of a plant (roots, stem, leaves, flowers), and Year 2 asks children to observe and describe how seeds and bulbs grow into mature plants, and how plants need water, light and a suitable temperature.

The words to use: the seed germinates when it takes in water and is warm enough. The first root (the radicle) always comes out first and turns to grow down, because roots respond to gravity. The shoot grows up. A young plant with its first leaves is a seedling. A broad bean or runner bean in a clear jar, pressed against wet kitchen paper, shows the root in about 2 to 5 days in a warm room.

Common mistakes: thinking the shoot comes first; thinking a seed needs light to start (beans, peas and sunflowers germinate in the dark under the soil, though a few tiny seeds such as lettuce do need light); thinking the seed eats soil (it lives on its own food store until the leaves can make food); and thinking an upside down seed will grow the wrong way. Be careful: a seed in a cold fridge stays asleep, so warmth matters as much as water.

In the lab your child drags a seed into a pot and waters it, slides the days along to watch a bean grow in a glass jar (lying the right way, on its side and upside down), carries a wet pot to a sunny window, a dark cupboard and a cold fridge, puts root, shoot and leaf labels on a seedling, and lines up the life story. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Push a bean between wet kitchen paper and the side of a clear jar. Keep the paper damp and check each morning. Ask: which came out first, the root or the shoot? Which way is the root growing?

visual.caption: Root or shoot? Drag each card to a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: plant and water a seed, watch a bean's root and shoot grow in a jar, find what wakes a seed, label root, shoot and leaf, and order the life story.

practice.prompt: Mo plants a bean in a jar. What comes out of the bean first?
practice.hint: The seed needs a drink before it can grow up. Which part drinks?
practice.explain: The root comes out first and grows down to drink water. The shoot comes next.

practice.prompt: Ella plants {n} seeds. Then she plants 2 more. How many seeds has she planted?
practice.hint: Start at {n} and count on 2 more.
practice.explain: {n} seeds and 2 more make {=n+2} seeds. Each one needs water and warmth to wake up.

practice.prompt: A bean is planted upside down. Which way does its root grow?
choices: It grows up to the sky
practice.hint: Think of the bean in the jar. Where did every root go?
practice.explain: A root always turns to grow down, so an upside down bean still sends its root down into the soil.

practice.prompt: A bean shoot has {n} leaves. Then 2 new leaves open. How many leaves now?
practice.hint: Count the leaves you have, then count on 2.
practice.explain: {n} leaves and 2 new ones make {=n+2} leaves. Leaves need light to grow green.

pool.prompt: What does a seed need to wake up and start growing?
pool.hint: Think of the pot in the cold fridge. Why did it stay asleep?
pool.explain: A seed needs water and warmth to start. Most seeds can start in the dark, under the soil.

pool.prompt: A wet bean sits in a cold fridge for a week. What happens?
pool.hint: Is a fridge warm or cold?
pool.explain: The fridge is too cold, so the seed stays asleep. It needs warmth as well as water.

pool.prompt: Which part grows up to the light?
pool.hint: One part goes down to drink. The other goes up. Which goes up?
pool.explain: The shoot grows up to the light and its leaves open at the top. The root grows down.

pool.prompt: Which comes just after the seed?
pool.hint: What came out of the bean in the jar first?
pool.explain: First the root comes out of the seed. Then the shoot and leaves make a seedling, then a big plant.

pool.prompt: Where do new bean seeds come from?
pool.hint: Look at the last picture in the life story. What does the big plant make?
pool.explain: A big bean plant grows pods with new beans inside. Plant a bean and the life story starts again.

pool.prompt: You put {n} beans in a warm pot and {k} beans in a cold fridge. Only the warm ones sprout. How many sprout?
pool.hint: The cold beans stay asleep. Count only the warm ones.
pool.explain: Only the {n} warm beans sprout. The {k} cold beans stay asleep, so {=n} beans sprout.

pool.prompt: A root is {n} blocks long. The next day it is 1 block longer. How long is it now?
pool.explain: {n} blocks and 1 more is {=n+1} blocks. The root keeps growing down into the soil.

pool.prompt: Can a bean start to grow in a dark cupboard if it is wet and warm?
choices: Yes, it can start in the dark
No, it needs light to start
pool.hint: A seed under the soil is in the dark. Does it still grow?
pool.explain: Yes. A wet, warm bean starts in the dark. Its leaves come out pale, so it needs light to grow green.
